text.text_excerpt: Elio's is great! It's well hidden at the back of a dead end behind Felipe's. The parking lot is tight and I've definitely had to do a 15-point turn to exit in the full lot before. Try to park next to sedans because if you're next to a truck, you won't have space to back up safely. My husband loves their beer selection- they post on Facebook when they get new stuff in, too. They are great for recommendations- I always buy something new when I go. They have some stuff on tap so bring a growler! Their wine selection is amazing. We go there sometimes when we are bored just to find something new. They're conveniently located across Claiborne from Tulane so their mixer collection is well stocked.

I'm always looking for new places to buy craft beer here in New Orleans. As you already know my go to store is Steins Deli but I'm always looking for places to promote here on the site. Just because I like Stein's doesn't mean you will or maybe you will be looking for something closer to you. Not too long ago I was posting stuff about the Parish Brewing Grand Reserve and Andrew Pollack pointed out that Elio's Wine Warehouse had some. Now as a Tulane grad this came to me as a bit funny. I remember Elio's being the place to get your cheap beer while in college. I have never thought of Elio's as a place to go to get good craft beer. I was wrong. A "wine warehouse" sounds just wrong, doesn't it? But hey, I'm no wine snob, so I do just fine here. Actually wine snobs would be fooled by the name-they've got quite the selection of bottles by the case (not wines by the glass, natch). I like buying wines by the case. Don't judge. I happen to throw quite the soirée from time to time... Elio's is one of the few places in town to offer a variety of beers by the keg, too (domestic, craft, import). Check out their website because they practically give you directions on how to throw a damn party yourself.
